Two independent evidence types support it: runtime logs showing the exact TypeError in order-service (E-ac30816c978d4536) plus metrics showing ~98% order-service error rate (E-44b6820ebacf463a), and source reads confirming pricing.py line 3 permits discount=None while line 6 subtracts it plus the immutable contract test requiring None to act as 0 (E-538664f710274552, E-89899411236d4870). Clean infrastructure evidence rules out DB/cache/consumer causes. The mechanism and service are materially correct.

judgment.explanation: Ground truth is a Kafka consumer lag fault on notification-service: the notification consumer pauses processing and commits, causing end offsets to grow while committed offsets stay fixed. The submitted diagnosis declares UNKNOWN / no live root cause, attributing signals to cumulative counters from past injections, and points at inventory-service as affected. This contradicts the ground truth mechanism and service. Although the diagnosis does note a small Kafka lag (180) and mentions the notification consumer in passing, it dismisses it as benign rather than identifying the actual injected fault, and it explicitly concludes no live root cause exists — the opposite of the ground-truth conclusion. Evidence cited (one Kafka snapshot plus other metrics) is a single useful source without the required independent supporting observations of end-offset growth vs fixed committed offset. Category and mechanism are therefore materially wrong.
